title: repair_mesh leaves 9-23 folded faces on crawfish IMG_4110-4112, so quad_layout refuses them as pleated
user-messages: [recalled] create ticket for unblocking crawfish and get agent started on it
description: quad_layout refuses the crawfish scans IMG_4110, IMG_4111 and IMG_4112 as pleated surfaces: after repair_mesh 9-23 faces are still folded (a face folded back over its neighbour), a second repair_mesh pass leaves 1-2, and smoothing before the layout makes it worse (8). Found by CRAW-129 (rings from the seamless parametrization), whose crawfish comparison needs the quad layout's seamless map on these scans; its proposal DSLs are ready in CRAW-129's worktree tmp/crawfish_41xx_iso_rings.dsl. The scans are in ${IXDAR_DATA_ROOT}/crawfish/IMG_41xx.glb (data root = home folder on this machine). MeshUnfold (added in CRAW-114 for the T-Rex skull's 176 folded slivers) is the existing unfold step inside repair_mesh; find why it leaves these folds, and why a second pass helps, and fix it so one repair_mesh pass unfolds completely.
definition-of-done:
1. One repair_mesh pass leaves no folded face on IMG_4109 to IMG_4118, and quad_layout lays out IMG_4110, IMG_4111 and IMG_4112 (patches, cones, quads reported).
2. Why MeshUnfold left the folds is explained on the ticket, and the fix is at that cause.
3. The T-Rex skull and all 11 quad-layout suite models keep their quads, patches and cones through repair_mesh + quad_layout.
4. Build checkstyle-green; MeshRepairTest covers the clear-and-refill stage on an edge with four faces, an hourglass vertex and a figure-eight hole.

5. MeshRepairReport keeps the two counters the repair_mesh report prints for the one clear-and-refill stage: tangleDeletedFaceCount (faces cleared round the split's copies left on one surface, before the fill) and foldClearedFaceCount (faces cleared round the folds and zero-length edges the unfold leaves, before each refill).

6. CrawfishMeshRepairBenchmark.repairOneScan asserts 0 folded faces, 0 zero-length edges and no vertex outside the scan's bounding box by more than a mean edge.

Accepts perf regression CrawfishMeshRepairBenchmark: master's 0.018 s is the time to fail on a hard-coded /home/acw scan path; this change points the benchmark at the data root, so it now runs the whole repair (4.6 s including load) instead of erroring.
testing-plan: 1. repair_mesh then a fold count on all ten crawfish scans before and after. 2. quad_layout on IMG_4110-4112. 3. Skull and suite counts unchanged.
changes-made: MeshRepair gains one clear-and-refill stage (clearAround): the split's copies left on one surface are cleared before the fill, and the folds and zero-length edges master's centroid MeshUnfold leaves are cleared and refilled a ring wider each round until none is left or a refill leaves a hole open; MeshUnfold now averages only the moving vertices' rings, which made it about 3x faster per round. Ten crawfish scans: 0 folds, 0 zero-length edges, 0 holes, 0 vertices outside, 1.1-2.6 s per scan.
